title: From Shallow Humor to Metaphor: Towards Label-Free Harmful Meme Detection via LMM Agent Self-Improvement

problem.claim: Harmful memes pose risks to public health and stability.

gap.claim: Existing detection methods depend heavily on large-scale labeled data, requiring substantial manual annotation and limiting adaptability to evolving harmful content.

contributions.claim: ALARM is a label-free harmful meme detection framework powered by LMM agent self-improvement.
ALARM uses Confidence-based Explicit Meme Identification to isolate explicit memes and assign pseudo-labels.
ALARM introduces Pairwise Learning Guided Agent Self-Improvement, reorganizing explicit memes into positive-negative contrastive pairs to refine an LMM agent that derives high-level detection cues.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three diverse datasets demonstrate superior performance and strong adaptability to newly evolved memes.
The authors report that ALARM outperforms label-driven methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Harmful memes are presented as a public-health and societal-stability risk.
Existing approaches rely on extensive labeled data and manual annotation, reducing adaptability to evolving content.
The paper presents ALARM, a label-free framework using LMM agent self-improvement.
ALARM identifies and pseudo-labels explicit memes, forms contrastive pairs, and uses them to derive cues for handling more complex memes.
The authors report strong performance and adaptability across three datasets, including results exceeding label-driven methods, and suggest scalability for novel harmful-meme forms and topics.

source_observation.claim: The framework uses relatively explicit memes as pseudo-labeled contrastive training material for improving detection of more complex memes.

interpretation.claim: Observable or easier examples may provide self-generated supervision for adapting to harder cases.

application.claim: For evolving multimodal detection tasks, organize accessible examples into explicit positive-negative contrasts to help a model derive transferable cues.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy works beyond the reported harmful-meme setting or without sufficient explicit examples.
